subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser-tool slice should maintainers sponsor first from this umbrella: state/readiness signals, model-facing batch/schema exposure, CDP element inspection, CAPTCHA signaling, or post-fill verification?
rationale: Current main already implements some lower-level mechanics, but the remaining asks change model-facing browser API behavior and agent state semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent product slice alone.

options.title: Prioritize state/readiness signals
options.body: Split stale-ref, snapshot-readiness, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker, and action-result-diff signaling into focused maintainer-owned issues or PRs first.

options.title: Expose batch/schema first
options.body: Sponsor a smaller model-facing batch/schema/docs slice that advertises and tests the existing lower-level batch support before broader state-signal work.

options.title: Close after partial implementation
options.body: Treat selector actions, ARIA ref guidance, selector waits, click delay, and lower-level batch support as sufficient despite the remaining requested signals.

recommendation.title: Prioritize state/readiness signals
recommendation.body: Split stale-ref, snapshot-readiness, CAPTCHA/manual-blocker, and action-result-diff signaling into focused maintainer-owned issues or PRs first.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior partial browser action fix and have the clearest recent history on the selector/batch route contract.
